$comment: Requests to serve (decisions 67, 68, and 71). Rock's Involvement connection type keeps its name and gets a real description and icon. Each opportunity places people on its serving team (serving.json) at the requester's campus. These are request statuses, not the person connection statuses in connection-statuses.json.

connectionType.name: Involvement
connectionType.description: People who want to get involved by serving. A connector follows up, helps each person find a team that fits, and places them on that team at their campus.

$requestStatusesComment: Rock ships No Contact and In Progress; the sample church adds the two onboarding steps between them and serving. Colors show on the connection board.

requestStatuses.name: No Contact
requestStatuses.description: A new request. No one has reached out yet.

requestStatuses.name: In Progress
requestStatuses.description: A connector has reached out and is helping the person find a team that fits.

requestStatuses.name: Background Check
requestStatuses.description: Waiting on a background check before the person can serve.

requestStatuses.name: Shadowing
requestStatuses.description: Serving alongside an experienced volunteer before joining the team.

$placementComment: Connecting someone adds them to the team with this role and status. Pending is Rock's default; the team leader makes them Active after onboarding (decision 71).
$attributeOptionsComment: Rock ships three opportunity attributes on Involvement, used as filters on the public Serve page. Preference Area's options become the serving areas; keys 1 and 2 keep their meaning (Children's and First Impressions). Each opportunity's attributes give its values by attribute key.

requests.$comment: Requests to serve (decision 74). Every volunteer who joined in the last historyDays came through a connected request that ends on the day they joined. Active and inactive requests come from people who are not serving, in the profile's state mix around the connected ones. A few people per campus connected in the last few weeks and wait on the team leader as Pending (decision 71). The Cast's own requests are in their household files.
requests.$connectorComment: Share of requests with a connector, by state. Active requests waiting on a background check or shadowing always have one. Together they give about the profile's 35% (connections.pctWithConnector). The connector is the team's leader at the person's campus.

$opportunitiesComment: Each opportunity's Name is its team's name from serving.json; publicName is the role a person takes on. The first three keep Rock's Guids. In list order.

opportunities.summary: Be the first friendly face people see. Greeters welcome guests at the doors and help them find their way.
opportunities.description:
A warm welcome sets the tone for someone's whole morning. Greeters open doors, say hello, and help guests find the kids area, the worship center, or the coffee.

What you'll do: welcome people at the main entrance or the kids entrance, answer questions, and walk first-time guests where they need to go.

Time: about 45 minutes before and during one service, once or twice a month.

A good fit if: you like meeting people and remembering names. Families and couples often serve together.

Training: a short walkthrough with a team leader on your first Sunday.

opportunities.summary: Help people find a seat and keep the service running smoothly, from the first song to the offering.
opportunities.description:
Walking into a full room can feel overwhelming. Ushers notice who needs help and make it easy to find a seat.

What you'll do: help people find seats, hand out what the service needs, receive the offering, and help serve communion.

Time: one service, once or twice a month.

A good fit if: you're calm, attentive, and happy to help in the background.

Training: shadow an experienced usher for one Sunday.

opportunities.summary: Help kids from the nursery through 6th grade learn about Jesus in a safe, fun place.
opportunities.description:
Every Sunday, kids hear that God loves them from people who know their names. Kids volunteers make that happen in every room, from the nursery to 6th grade.

What you'll do: welcome kids to their room, lead a small group or activity, and care for babies and toddlers in the nursery.

Time: one service, about twice a month. Lessons are ready for you each week.

A good fit if: you love kids. No teaching experience is needed.

Training: a background check and our kids safety training, then shadow a room leader for a Sunday.

opportunities.summary: Sing or play on the team that leads the church in worship each Sunday.
opportunities.description:
The Worship Team helps the whole room sing together. We need vocalists and players for keys, guitar, bass, and drums.

What you'll do: learn the week's songs, join a Thursday rehearsal, and lead worship at the services you're scheduled for.

Time: a rehearsal and a Sunday morning, about twice a month.

A good fit if: you sing or play with some experience and enjoy serving as part of a band.

Training: a short, friendly audition with the worship leader, then a rehearsal with the team.

opportunities.summary: Run sound, lights, slides, cameras, or the livestream. No experience needed.
opportunities.description:
Behind every service is a team that makes sure people can hear, see, and follow along, in the room and online.

What you'll do: run sound, lights, slides, a camera, or the livestream from the production booth.

Time: about two hours on a Sunday morning, once or twice a month.

A good fit if: you like technology or want to learn it. Many of our best volunteers started with no experience.

Training: hands-on training at one position at a time, alongside a team leader.

opportunities.summary: Walk with 7th through 12th graders as they grow in faith, one Sunday conversation at a time.
opportunities.description:
Students need adults who show up, listen, and care. Student leaders build friendships with the same group of students week after week.

What you'll do: lead a small group conversation after the message, and check in with your students during the week.

Time: the student service every week, plus a few events each year.

A good fit if: you're 21 or older and want to invest in the next generation.

Training: a background check, our student safety training, and a meeting with the student pastor.

opportunities.summary: Pray with people before and after services, in the prayer room or at the front after the message.
opportunities.description:
Sometimes the most important part of a Sunday is the prayer afterward. Prayer partners are ready to listen and pray with anyone who asks.

What you'll do: pray with people in the prayer room or at the front after the service, and keep what you hear in confidence.

Time: one service, once or twice a month.

A good fit if: you're a good listener and comfortable praying aloud with others.

Training: a short training on praying with others and caring for people in hard seasons.

opportunities.summary: Use your medical training to care for anyone who needs help during a service.
opportunities.description:
With hundreds of people on campus, someone may need first aid. The First Aid Team is ready to respond calmly and quickly.

What you'll do: staff the first aid station, carry a radio, and care for injuries and medical needs until more help arrives.

Time: one service, about once a month.

A good fit if: you have current first aid and CPR certification, or medical training such as nursing or EMT work.

Training: an orientation to our station, radios, and emergency plan.
